definition: Whether a system that handles parts handles their combination, and across 5 sources the case where the archive's models most reliably fail. The cleanest measurement holds the parts fixed: on a benchmark where each task needs one commonsense step and one mathematical step, accuracy drops nearly 30 percent relative to solving the same steps in isolation, while humans show no such gap. A mechanistic source finds the same asymmetry inside a learned circuit -- extended training past overfitting produces a circuit that generalises out of distribution for comparison and fails for composition, so it is composition specifically that the learned structure does not carry. Two benchmarks in the set are built to require induced cascades or nested structure, one with automated contamination-resistant generation and controllable difficulty, which is the design the archive prefers for this property because the composition depth becomes a knob rather than a confound. One latent-reasoning source probes what its demonstration-bound operators can and cannot compose, which is the same question asked of a learned representation rather than of a benchmark.

evidence.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
evidence.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

evidence.note: Combines in-context learning through evolving recurrent memory with iterative reasoning in a continuous latent workspace that is never decoded into language, reaching 29.5% pass@2 on public ARC-AGI-1 at $0.0007 per task from 150M parameters, and then probes with controlled tasks what the resulting demonstration-bound operators can and cannot do.
evidence.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

evidence.note: Consolidates multiword-expression resources into one evaluation suite covering idioms, noun compounds and verbal constructions across extraction, classification and interpretation tasks.
evidence.title: Revisiting a Pain in the Neck: A Semantic Reasoning Benchmark for Language Models

evidence.note: A benchmark where each task needs one commonsense step and one math step, on which model accuracy drops nearly 30% relative to solving the steps in isolation while humans show no such gap.
evidence.title: AgentCoMa: A Compositional Benchmark Mixing Commonsense and Mathematical Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios

evidence.note: An inductive-reasoning benchmark from historical linguistics that requires inducing cascades of string-rewrite programs, with automated contamination-resistant generation and controllable difficulty.
evidence.title: PBEBench: A Multi-Step Programming by Examples Reasoning Benchmark inspired by Historical Linguistics

name: compositional generalization
